name: Dongjae Kang
bio: is an MPA candidate in Technology Policy and Innovation at Columbia University, with a B.S. in Industrial and Systems Engineering from KAIST. As an intern at the UN Statistics Division, he leads development of a companion to UN Statistical Commission session reports that links each decision to the discussion behind it. He co-first-authored CrisisNews, a 93,250-article dataset presented at News Futures (CHI 2025), and builds PRISM, a news platform publishing daily public-affairs briefs with source provenance across US and Korean media.

name: Sze Wing (Hesper) Lui
bio: is an MPA candidate at Columbia University in the Technology Policy and Innovation concentration, with a minor in Cybersecurity. She previously worked at MSCI, supporting ESG and climate-related communications, and conducted research at the Chinese Academy of Sciences on technology-enabled interventions and the cultural factors that may influence neurodivergence in young people. Her current research examines legitimacy laundering.

name: Sara Shibata
bio: studies International Security and Diplomacy with a minor in Technology Policy at Columbia University and is Communications Director of the Digital and Cyber Program run by SIPA Cyber. She has worked at Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. She holds a Master of Public Policy from the University of Tokyo, where she researched social media civic participation among Japanese youth.

name: Sneha Shree Saikia
bio: is a Master of International Affairs student at Columbia University in International Security and Diplomacy, with a minor in Technology Policy. Saikia studied Philosophy and Conflict Transformation and Peacebuilding at the University of Delhi, and as an intern in UNDP's Crisis Bureau worked with the DDR and Stabilization teams on designing information management systems and AI tools for practitioners and country offices.

name: Xuefei (Sophie) Ren
bio: is an MPA candidate in Technology Policy and Innovation at Columbia University, with an academic background in international business and psychology. She has worked in management consulting, robotics strategy, and responsible-AI entrepreneurship across North America and China. She has supported cross-functional digital product initiatives, advised an emerging companion robotics company on product and market strategy, and co-founded an ethical technology initiative advancing responsible AI and data transparency.

name: Puyu (Irene) Cui
bio: is a master's student in Computer and Information Science at the University of Pennsylvania, with a background in computer science, statistics, and finance. She works on AI and machine learning, including natural language processing, reinforcement learning, and AI agents.

name: Crystal Yang
bio: is an MIA candidate in Technology Policy and Innovation at Columbia SIPA and is admitted as a solicitor in Australia. She holds a combined Bachelor degree in Law and Arts from the University of Sydney, held legal and compliance roles at the Australian Taxation Office, and led public programs advancing free knowledge on the internet at Wikimedia NYC.

name: Fio Wibawa
bio: is a dual-degree candidate in Columbia University's Master of International Affairs and the University of Tokyo's Master of Public Policy International Program. At Columbia, Wibawa concentrated in Technology Policy and Innovation with a focus on AI governance, and at Tokyo follows the Public Management and International Relations stream on law, policy, and emerging technologies.
affiliation: The University of Tokyo · Columbia University

name: Zifu (Tyler) Qin
bio: is a Ph.D. researcher in Systems Engineering at Cornell University, working on multimedia forensics, computer vision, signal processing, and trustworthy AI. Qin's research develops computational and forensic methods for detecting and localizing manipulated visual content, including deepfakes, under real-world media transformations. Qin also participated in NSF I-Corps, exploring how to translate media authentication technologies into practice.
